name: The renouncers
note: Sixty REFORM events. Councils and schisms, the bhakti movements region by region, the Sufi and Sikh traditions, and the caste question carried as a single thread from one late Rigvedic hymn to Article 17 — twenty-one events on THR.THE_CASTE_QUESTION, which had almost none.

events.title: The Purusha Sukta states four varnas, once, in a late hymn
events.evidence: Rigveda 10.90, whose language and position in the tenth mandala mark it as among the latest material in the collection.
events.note: One hymn, late, in a collection of a thousand. Everything after argues with it.

events.title: Varna and jati come apart: four categories, and hundreds of groups
events.evidence: The Dharmasutras, which try to fit named occupational and regional groups into the four-fold scheme and produce mixed categories to do it.
events.note: The theory has four boxes. The society has hundreds of groups. The gap is where the argument lives.

events.title: The Buddha argues that birth does not make a brahmin
events.evidence: The Vasettha and Ambattha suttas, which put the argument in the mouth of brahmin interlocutors and have them lose it.

events.title: The sangha admits across varna, and a barber ordains before princes
events.evidence: The Vinaya's account of Upali's ordination ahead of the Shakya nobles, so that they would have to bow to him.

events.title: The bhikkhuni order is founded, on conditions
events.evidence: The Cullavagga's account of Mahapajapati's request, its refusal, and the eight garudhammas attached to the eventual assent.
events.note: Admitted, and subordinated in the same paragraph. The text records both.

events.title: The Therigatha: seventy-three women record why they left
events.evidence: The collection itself, the earliest surviving anthology of women's writing anywhere.

events.title: Makkhali Gosala teaches niyati — everything is already settled
events.evidence: The Samannaphala Sutta and the Jain Bhagavati Sutra, both hostile witnesses, which is all we have.
events.note: A whole school known only through the writings of people who thought it was wrong.

events.title: Exclusion hardens: the first texts on ritual pollution by contact
events.evidence: The later Dharmasutras and the Manusmriti's chapters on mixed castes, and Faxian's report of signalling on approach.

events.title: Bhakti opens the temple door in argument if not always in fact
events.evidence: The Nayanar and Alvar hagiographies, which include Nandanar and Tiruppan Alvar, and the tension the stories themselves record.

events.title: Basava's Anubhava Mantapa seats artisans and brahmins together
events.evidence: The vachanas themselves, and the violence that followed the inter-caste marriage the movement sanctioned.

events.title: Ramananda takes disciples without regard to birth
events.evidence: The Bhaktamal tradition and the disciple lists that name Ravidas, Kabir and Sena.

events.title: Ravidas describes Begampura, a city without sorrow or tax or caste
events.evidence: His verses in the Guru Granth Sahib and the Rajasthani manuscript tradition.
events.note: A leatherworker describes a city with no grading of men. It is a utopia, and it is a critique.

events.title: Nanak makes the shared kitchen a condition of the congregation
events.evidence: The institution of langar and pangat, and the janamsakhi accounts of Nanak eating with whoever came.

events.title: Chokhamela sings outside the temple he is not allowed to enter
events.evidence: His abhangas, and his samadhi's position at the threshold of the Pandharpur temple.

events.title: Narayana Guru consecrates a temple, and is asked by what right
events.evidence: The Aruvippuram consecration and the notice he put up: one caste, one religion, one God for man.

events.title: The Vaikom satyagraha opens the roads around a temple
events.evidence: The satyagraha's records, the Travancore state's concession on three of four roads, and the 1936 Temple Entry Proclamation that followed.

events.title: Jyotirao and Savitribai Phule open a school for girls and for the excluded
events.evidence: The school records at Bhide Wada, Pune, and Gulamgiri, published 1873.
events.note: A woman teaching, in 1848, in a country where most men could not read.

events.title: The Self-Respect movement holds weddings without priests
events.evidence: The Suyamariyathai marriage form, and the 1967 amendment that made it legally valid.

events.title: The Mahad satyagraha drinks from a public tank
events.evidence: The Chavdar tank action, the court case that followed, and the public burning of the Manusmriti in December.

events.title: The Poona Pact: separate electorates traded for reserved seats
events.evidence: The agreement itself, signed under the pressure of a fast unto death, and the Assembly debates that followed.
events.note: Both parties described it afterwards as a defeat. The game should present it that way.

events.title: The Constituent Assembly accepts the abolition of untouchability as a fundamental right
events.evidence: The Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee report of April 1947 and the Assembly's clause-by-clause debate, including the argument over whether the word should be defined or left to the courts.
events.note: It becomes Article 17 in 1949, two years after the campaign ends. The last thing the game shows you is an argument still in progress.

events.title: The first council recites the canon back to itself
events.evidence: The Vinaya's account of the recitation at Rajagriha, and the division of the canon between Ananda and Upali.

events.title: The second council splits over ten small rules
events.evidence: The Vinaya accounts, which disagree about the ten points and agree about the split.
events.note: A schism over whether a monk may accept coins. Small rules are never small.

events.title: The Mahasanghika separate, and the eighteen schools begin
events.evidence: The doxographies of the Sthavira and Mahasanghika traditions, which name each other's errors.

events.title: The third council, and the missions that follow it
events.evidence: The Sri Lankan chronicles, and Ashoka's schism edict at Sanchi, Sarnath and Kausambi.

events.title: Ashoka's schism edict threatens to unfrock a monk who splits the order
events.evidence: The minor pillar edict at three sites, which orders the offender put in white cloth and out of the residence.
events.note: A king legislating monastic discipline. The state has opinions about the sangha.

events.title: The Jain council at Pataliputra, and the first division
events.evidence: The Svetambara account of a twelve-year famine, Bhadrabahu's migration south, and the disagreement about what was recovered.

events.title: Digambara and Svetambara harden into separate traditions
events.evidence: Two separate canonical positions, two commentarial traditions and, from this period, two distinct sculptural conventions.

events.title: The Valabhi council fixes the Svetambara canon in writing
events.evidence: The Svetambara tradition's own account, and the recension that follows it.

events.title: The fourth council under Kanishka, and Sanskrit displaces Prakrit
events.evidence: Xuanzang's account, and the shift to Sanskrit in the northwestern Buddhist textual record.

events.title: The Mahayana sutras appear, claiming to be older than they are
events.evidence: The Prajnaparamita literature, whose earliest Chinese translations date its circulation, and its own framing device.

events.title: Vajrayana takes shape in the eastern monasteries
events.evidence: The tantras and their Tibetan transmission lineages, and the Pala-period iconography at Ratnagiri and Nalanda.

events.title: Buddhism thins in India while it grows everywhere else
events.evidence: The end of the inscription and endowment record, against the continued Tibetan, Chinese and Southeast Asian traditions.
events.note: Argued for two centuries and unsettled. The game shows the positions and does not pick one.

events.title: The Nayanars sing Shiva in Tamil, and walk between temples
events.evidence: The Tevaram hymns and the temple inscriptions that endow their recitation.

events.title: The Alvars sing Vishnu, and one of the twelve is a woman
events.evidence: The Divya Prabandham, and Andal's Tiruppavai, still recited in Margazhi.

events.title: Shankara founds four mathas at the compass points
events.evidence: The matha traditions themselves and their succession lists, whose early portions are disputed.
events.note: An institution designed to outlive its founder. Twelve hundred years later it has.

events.title: The Virashaivas reject temple, priest and caste in one movement
events.evidence: The vachana corpus and the Basava Purana.

events.title: Madhva argues for difference against Shankara's identity
events.evidence: His commentaries and the Udupi matha tradition.

events.title: Jnaneshwar puts the Gita into Marathi and is expelled for it
events.evidence: The Jnaneshwari itself, and the tradition of his family's excommunication.

events.title: The Varkari pilgrimage to Pandharpur becomes an annual institution
events.evidence: The abhanga corpus, and the palkhi routes still walked.

events.title: Chaitanya's kirtan takes devotion into the street
events.evidence: The Chaitanya Charitamrita, and the Bengal Vaishnava institutional record.

events.title: Sankardev's Ekasarana and the namghar as a village institution
events.evidence: The borgeet and ankiya nat corpus, and the namghar network across the Brahmaputra valley.
events.note: A prayer house that is also the village assembly. Devotion with a constitution.

events.title: Mirabai leaves a court to sing, and the court cannot get her back
events.evidence: Her padas in the Rajasthani and Braj traditions, and their inclusion in the Guru Granth Sahib.

events.title: Lal Ded's vakhs pass into Kashmiri speech and stay there
events.evidence: The vakhs, transmitted orally for centuries before collection, and quoted as proverb.

events.title: Namdev carries Marathi abhangas north into Punjab
events.evidence: His verses in both the Marathi tradition and the Guru Granth Sahib.

events.title: Annamacharya's keertanas are engraved on copper and sealed in a wall
events.evidence: The copper plates recovered from the Tirumala temple in 1922, some thirteen thousand songs.
events.note: Sealed in a room for four hundred years. Redundancy by accident.

events.title: Purandara Dasa sets the Carnatic teaching sequence still used
events.evidence: The graded exercises attributed to him, which every student still begins with.

events.title: The Chishti khanqahs open their kitchens to whoever comes
events.evidence: The malfuzat literature, the Ajmer and Delhi dargah endowments, and the sama' controversy.

events.title: Kabir refuses both temple and mosque, and both claim him after
events.evidence: The three recensions of his verse, and the tradition that both communities claimed the body.

events.title: The Sikh panth takes institutional form: sangat, langar, and a line of Gurus
events.evidence: The janamsakhis, the Goindval pothis, and the succession from Nanak.

events.title: The Khalsa is instituted at Anandpur
events.evidence: The Sikh chronicles and the surviving hukamnamas.

events.title: Shakta and Tantric practice spreads through Bengal, Assam and Kashmir
events.evidence: The tantric corpus, the Kamakhya tradition, and the Pala-period iconography.

events.title: The Nath siddhas cut across religion and caste and leave verse behind
events.evidence: The Gorakh bani, the Charyapada, and the Nath monastic network from Nepal to Gujarat.

events.title: The Mahanubhava sect writes prose in Marathi and encrypts it
events.evidence: The Lilacharitra, and the sect's sakala cipher scripts.
events.note: They wrote their scripture in code to keep it from outsiders. It nearly worked too well.

events.title: The Srivaishnavas divide over whether grace requires effort
events.evidence: The Vadakalai and Tenkalai commentarial traditions, and the temple litigation between them.

events.title: The Lingayat mathas become landholding institutions
events.evidence: The matha inscription and grant record across the Kannada country.

events.title: The Brahmo Samaj argues for reform from inside the texts
events.evidence: The Samaj's trust deed, and Rammohan Roy's translations and tracts.

events.title: The Arya Samaj argues for reform by returning to the Vedas
events.evidence: The Satyarth Prakash, and the Samaj's school network.

events.title: Sati is prohibited by regulation, after argument on both sides in Sanskrit
events.evidence: Bengal Regulation XVII, and the petitions for and against, several of them citing the same texts.

events.title: The Widow Remarriage Act, argued through the shastras
events.evidence: Act XV of 1856, and Vidyasagar's tracts marshalling scriptural authority for it.

events.title: Ambedkar and half a million others take Buddhist vows at Nagpur
events.evidence: The announcement of intent at Yeola in 1935 and the conversion at Nagpur, with its twenty-two vows.
events.note: The oldest renouncer tradition in the country, taken up again to answer the oldest question in it.
